The old test did depend on `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`, and the fixed one doesn't. I ran the proof with `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2`, the value a CI re-run supplies.

**Why it depended on it.** The test builds the child process environment from `process.env` and strips some variables first. In the old version (`593679a5`) the filter was `/^(CEZ_|HSQ_|GITHUB_ACTIONS$|ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_|NODE_AUTH_TOKEN)/`. That removed `GITHUB_ACTIONS` but not `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`, so the variable passed through from the workflow. `scripts/release-snapshot.mjs:62` reads it and adds the attempt number to the version when it matches `/^\d+$/`. The test never set it itself.

**What the fix changed (`a9a1fbf9`).**
- The filter now strips every `GITHUB_*` variable.
- The test sets `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT: '1'` explicitly, so the expected versions don't depend on the runner.

**The proof.** I ran `squeal proof scripts/release-identity.test.mjs --base a9a1fbf9^ --case test --env GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2`. It ran the old test file against the current code and the fixed file against the same code, both with that variable set.

| Side | Result |
|---|---|
| Old test (`a9a1fbf9^`), attempt=2 | Fails with the wrong version |
| Fixed test (`HEAD`), attempt=2 | Passes |
| Old test without the variable | Passes, so the failure comes from the variable alone |

Verdict: 1 proven, 0 not red, 0 red for another reason, 0 not green.

The failures in the old run are the ones you saw on CI re-runs:
- nightly: got `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9.2`, expected `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9`
- PR: got `1.2.3-pr7.9.2`, expected `1.2.3-pr7.9`

The same assertion at `scripts/release-identity.test.mjs:96` failed for each of these channels.

The run was in temporary checkouts, so your tree is untouched.
